real_name: Javed Khanani — real name kept in film
real_life_notes: Altaf Khanani's brother and operational partner in the Khanani money laundering network. Operated within Karachi's financial underworld as the Pakistan-side executor of the hawala operations. Died on 4 December 2016 in Karachi — reportedly fell from the fourth floor of an under-construction building. Manner of death disputed: accident, suicide, or targeted killing. The timing — 26 days after India's demonetisation on 8 November 2016 — is the basis for the film's central thesis about demonetisation as a financial-kinetic weapon.
film_role: Film 2 — Javed is the on-the-ground Karachi operator of the Khanani network. His death in December 2016 is depicted in the film as either a consequence of the financial collapse triggered by demonetisation or as a targeted operation. The film likely presents it as the latter.
objective: Execute day-to-day hawala operations; maintain ISI financial relationships; manage Karachi-side FICN distribution

real_death.circumstances: Fell from fourth floor of an under-construction building in Karachi. Officially: accident or suicide. Speculation: targeted killing linked to FICN network collapse post-demonetisation.
real_death.context: 26 days after India's demonetisation. His death created speculation about 'financial pressure and unsustainable liabilities' on the hawala network.

demonetisation_link: The film's thesis: demonetisation on 8 November 2016 didn't just shock Indian citizens — it ruptured the financial arteries of Pakistan's covert operators. The high-quality FICN stockpiles suddenly became worthless. Javed's death is presented as the human consequence of this financial disruption.
